newsitem.title: USA: U.S., France trying to aid Zaire peace, Millon says.
newsitem.headline: U.S., France trying to aid Zaire peace, Millon says.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon said on Tuesday that the United States and France are trying to aid a peace agreement in Zaire.

"Yes, there is a common U.S.-French approach as far as trying to reach peace and achieve a positive change, change toward stability in Zaire," Millon said before a meeting with Defence Secretary William Cohen.

"The U.S. and France are coordinating their diplomacy so that (rebel leader Laurent) Kabila and Mobutu (President Mobutu Sese Seko) can reach an agreement on a government that will satisfy what the people expect from it," Millon said through an interpreter.

Cohen did not reply directly when asked if the United States and other countries were trying to help achieve a Zaire peace agreement, saying "obviously there are countries who are concerned about the situation in Zaire."

The State Department said on Monday that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright had sent Mobutu a letter urging him to seek a ceasefire and establish a negotiating team or designate a person who can engage in negotiations on behalf of the Zaire government.
